description: We are ZERO POINT — SPHEREx Explorer, a team led by Yash Petkar with members Pratik Lokande and Eshaan Jadhav. We aim to build an interactive platform to explore real SPHEREx infrared observations and astronomical data for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We welcome teammates skilled in astronomy, Python, AI/ML, data analysis, web development, and visualization. We value teamwork, curiosity, and scientific thinking.
summary:
SkyMotion — SPHEREx Explorer

SkyMotion is a scientific exploration platform designed to help users investigate observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission. It provides an interface for searching astronomical observations by sky coordinates, inspecting FITS image data and metadata, exploring observation timelines, and comparing observations from different epochs.
The project aims to make SPHEREx data more accessible by bringing astronomical data exploration and visualization into one application. Users can examine scientific image products, inspect available quality and variance information, and investigate potential changes between observations.
SkyMotion uses a React and TypeScript frontend with a Python FastAPI backend and astronomical data-processing libraries. It is designed around NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) SPHEREx data products.
The long-term goal is to provide an accessible scientific workflow for exploring the changing infrared sky and supporting the investigation of moving or variable astronomical sources.
details:
SkyMotion is a web-based astronomical exploration platform designed to help users investigate observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission.

The application provides a scientific dashboard, coordinate-based sky search, FITS Field Explorer, observation timeline, comparison interface, change-detection workflow, spectral analysis section, and SPHEREx archive browser.

Users can inspect astronomical FITS images and associated metadata, including observation identifiers, sky coordinates, detector information, observation dates, image dimensions and available quality information. The platform also includes an IRSA Live Search interface that sends coordinate-based archive queries through a Python FastAPI backend.

The frontend is developed using React, TypeScript and Vite. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, with scientific libraries including Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, Photutils, Reproject and Shapely.

SkyMotion aims to make infrared astronomical data easier to explore through a unified scientific workflow. An important design consideration is scientific reliability: observations must be checked for compatibility, coordinate alignment, wavelength information and data quality before meaningful comparisons can be made.

The project is a prototype. Live archive querying, complete observation importing and scientific validation of multi-epoch comparisons require further verification.
